verdicts.reason: Low-angle drift past the user with real depth: the desk is in the foreground and the rack and vaults are in the background. A spot pool gives key and rim, and the laptop slides in. Faults: the CLIENT01 label is cropped by the frame edge in _a and _b, and the caption sits on the focal USER in _b and _c.

The amber pulse leads the camera along the floor channel with strong parallax: the user's chair passes in the foreground and the rack arrives in the background. The caption stays during travel. Motion reads as cinematic.
Arrival push-in on the server with an amber listener light and spot light. The focal subject is clear and sits in front of the CA vaults and the AD pillar.

A pull-back reveals the whole space and the pulse dies out of the channel, which is a good staging idea. The focal self-signed card is tiny, and the 'Self-signed' and 'Unverified' chips cover it. A hard black void with a visible floor edge fills the top quarter of the frame.

An overhead swoop with a high-angle push onto the server as the RDPAuth badge drops in. The camera has parallax against the pki kiosk and the CA1 vault, and the badge has depth. The rdp01 label partly covers the badge.
The camera dives into the open chassis and the shallow depth of field isolates the key pair. The door opens physically. The interior is dark and murky, but the focal subject is clear.
Close-up with depth of field. The key drops into the safe, the lid closes and the lock motif is visible. The lighting inside is soft and flat-ish. There is little foreground or background layering.
The public key and the plate merge into a glass capsule through motion and light. The capsule is bright and clearly the focal subject. The caption overlaps the lower container.

The container flashes and a beam seals the capsule while the container stays put. The beam is a rigid straight white rod, which reads slightly as a connector, but it appears and retracts as light and the motion reads as film.

The camera pulls out of the chassis, the capsule exits to the outbound port and the AD pillar frames the shot, so staging is dimensional. The focal AD pillar is acceptable. Unidentified white ring and pill shapes stay inside the server beside the octagon plate. The rdp01 label drifts over the badge.
The capsule rolls along the lit cyan route and the camera follows and leads it into the vault. The motion is clear and the cyan route is correct. The vault is large and bright.

The camera pushes into the CA1 vault with a staggered check list. The vault interior is flat emissive cyan, and heavy noise speckles the surfaces. The 'Issuing CA 1' label and the check text collide, and the checks are drawn as floating text that partly occludes the capsule. This is borderline but still a 3D space.

The press descends, the capsule is consumed and a card is stamped as the camera orbits. This is object motion, not a diagram. The label overlaps the press, the check text is not cleared when the card appears, and the card is a plain light slab.

The card travels along the channel and docks into the server beside the key container. The camera follows with parallax of CA1, the AD pillar and CA2. The server label and the key and plate area are clear. A white ring and pill sit outside the container.

A crane-up reveal of a gold vault on a plinth with a glint on its seal. The root is warm, isolated, cable-free and monumental. The shot ends on a nearly static, frontal, centred hold. A black void fills the top 30%.

The desaturated, noisy flashback is clearly marked with 'Earlier:' text and is the only cut, between f1245 and f1246. The CA1 vault and the root plinth share the frame. The request and USB tag are tiny, about 7 px, and the CA=true band is not discernible. The live B-04.3 check list is still drawn inside the flashback vault. The result is murky but reads as cinema.

The cut out is clean and the pull-back is smooth. The dominant read is a root-to-CA1 node-link graph: a straight white line grows from the CA1 cert to the root seal, and the line stays on screen for the rest of the film. It is not gold-to-cyan. The scene is wide and top-down with small objects.

A new amber pulse crosses the whole floor and the camera glides to the client desk. The cards arrive above the desk with depth. The subject is small in a very wide shot, and the proof impression and transit are not readable at this size. A hard black horizon cuts the top third.

The cards dock upward into a vertical stack as the camera orbits the desk. The root card goes from dark to gold with an 'Installed earlier by policy' shimmer. This is staged in 3D with motion. The stack of three flat same-colour cards facing the camera is somewhat slide-like. The caption has dither noise.

Two large floating text chips ('Missing intermediate? AIA can fetch it', 'Fetching never creates trust') cut across the cert stack and carry the beat. The focal AIA kiosk is not visible. The shot reads as annotation on a slide, not as a staged moment.

A huge screen-space checklist HUD of text lines, large enough to cover the focal chain, covers the cards and the user. It is the main read of the beat, so the beat looks like a UI overlay or slide. The cards and desk shrink to thumbnails behind the text.

A very wide shot with the checklist HUD text still dominant. The CRL fetches and the focal CDP kiosk are tiny. 'OCSP if deployed' is partly clipped ('JCSP'). The meaningful action (the fetches) is not legible. A thin amber line spans the floor like a graph edge.

The channel turns green from the client outward and the camera trucks along it with a visible session window. The colour change is motivated and readable. The checklist HUD is still large in _c, and the caption is noisy.

The camera glides from the green channel through the space to WEB01 with parallax of the server, the AD pillar and the vaults. Depth is strong. A white root-to-CA1 line slashes across the frame and the labels overlap the focal server.

A push into the open WEB01 chassis and the same key, safe, capsule and seal grammar as B-03, so it is visually consistent. The ghosted double label ('WEB01' over 'WebServer-TLS') covers the top of the frame.

A stack of floating eligibility tags (Template published, Enrollment policy, Permissions, CA available, 'not published here') plus the overlapping WEB01, WebServer-TLS and rdp01 labels carry the beat. CA1 is dimmed teal, not muted grey. The camera swings fast through the label clutter and the focal AD is off-centre. Information is in text, not in light or motion.
The capsule travels along the violet route only to CA2 and the camera leads into the vault. The violet colour language is clear. The capsule is tiny among the overlapping labels in _a and _b.

The camera pushes inside the violet vault and the compressed checks are shown. The vault label is oversized and covers about 25% of the frame. The 'Name supplied in request' note overprints the 'Request meets template policy' check. The interior is flat violet with speckle noise.

The stamp and the return are fine in _a and _b, but the camera ends up on the WEB01 label plane, so a black label card fills most of _c. The server, the cert lock-in and the key area cannot be seen at all, and the beat ends in a broken frame.

_a is covered by the giant WEB01 label (about 70% of the frame), so the beat starts blind. The recovery is a pull-back to an overview of nodes joined by straight white lines (a CA node graph). The link to the root is white, not cyan or violet to gold, and it reads as a diagram edge.

Wide, then a push to the client with the pulse running through the world and the chain stack docking. The compressed check text is again oversized and covers the chain in _b. The long amber and green lines across the floor read as graph edges in _a, but camera motion and docking carry the beat.

The hero shot is a tree: the root on top with two straight white lines to CA1 and CA2, and cyan and violet lines to the servers. The trust links are white, not cyan and violet rising to gold. The cyan and violet lines run from the CAs to the servers, the opposite direction. Static straight connectors, a near-frontal composition, tiny servers, and the caption sits on the lower subject. It looks like a slide org chart.

The title card fades in over the settled hero while the world dims, then goes to a clean black end. The settle and fade are acceptable. The title plate crosses the root and the CA vaults in _b. The black void and floor edge are visible at the top.

findings.evidence: In B-08.2_c a black label plate with huge 'WEB01 / portal.1sn0s.lab' text fills about 60% of the frame. In B-08.3_a the label plate covers about 70% of the frame and the camera is clearly on its plane. The server, the cert lock-in, the key container and the root are hidden for about 40 frames. The B-08.2 and B-08.3 strips show the same.
findings.why: A broken or blind frame and no focal subject. The screen is occluded by its own label, and this is where the TLS certificate returns and locks beside the web server's key.
findings.direction: Route the camera and label billboards so no label plane gets near the lens. Keep the focal subject inside the safe frame and unoccluded through the whole beat hold.

findings.evidence: A straight white line joins the CA1 cert to the root seal from B-05.3 on and stays on screen unchanged in S6, S7 and S8. A second white line is added to CA2 in B-08.3. In B-09.2 the root, two CAs and two straight white lines form a tree graph.
findings.why: These are static straight connectors between nodes. The hero reads as an org chart. The spec asks for a trust link that grows and is a trust (issuer) relationship, with gold, cyan and violet paths converging.
findings.direction: Make the trust links curved, luminous, gradient (gold to cyan and gold to violet) paths that travel or pulse when introduced and then fade or settle into the objects. Do not leave a hard straight stick across the shots.

findings.evidence: The root-to-CA trust links are white. The cyan and violet lines instead run from the CA vaults down to the servers. The spec says two trust paths, cyan and violet, rise and converge in gold at the root. In B-07.3 CA1 is a dim teal, not the specified muted grey for an ineligible CA.
findings.why: The role colours do not follow the colour language. The path colours encode the wrong relationship (CA to server instead of the trust path up to the root), and ineligibility is not grey.
findings.direction: Colour the issuer links by CA (cyan, violet) rising to gold at the root, make the lower CA-to-server routes neutral channel colour, and dim the ineligible CA to the grey token in B-07.3.

findings.evidence: A large screen-space checklist of text lines (B-06.4) covers the cert chain and the client, and stays through B-06.5 and B-06.6. The AIA chips in B-06.3 are large text plates crossing the stack, and the eligibility tags in B-07.3 form a text stack. In B-06.4_b and B-06.4_c the chain is smaller than the text. The focal cards are shrunk to thumbnails.
findings.why: The information is carried by UI text, not by objects, light or motion. The shots read as slides or HUD overlays on top of a scene, which is the template-like look the brief forbids.
findings.direction: Make checks small in-world tick objects on or next to the focal subject, with the camera moving to each. Keep the text small enough that the focal subject stays at least 15% of the frame and unoccluded.

findings.evidence: Strong speckle noise is visible across vault walls and dark surfaces, much more than 2% of the signal. Caption plates have a double or dithered ghost edge, so text reads as 'The client vaudates the whole chain' and 'Issuing CA 1 verifies, then signs' is garbled at 960x540.
findings.why: Excess grain breaks the restraint threshold and degrades caption legibility.
findings.direction: Cap the noise or denoise before compositing and keep the caption layer outside the grain and haze pass. Use a clean caption plate.

findings.evidence: The focal self-signed card in B-02.2 is a few pixels wide and is covered by the 'Self-signed' and 'Unverified' chips. The focal CDP kiosk in B-06.5 and the proof in B-06.1 are tiny in wide shots. The focus distance is 17 to 30 m in these beats.
findings.why: No clear focal subject. The moment that matters is not photographed large enough to read, and depth of field is not doing the work.
findings.direction: Stage the focal subject much larger with a closer lens and shorter focus distance for these beats, and cut away from the full-floor pull-backs.

findings.evidence: The 'WEB01 / portal.1sn0s.lab' label and the 'WebServer-TLS' badge text overprint each other as a ghosted double. In B-07.3 and B-07.4 the 'rdp01.1sn0s.lab' label overlaps the 'RDPAuth' badge at the lower left.
findings.why: Required names are not readable or unoccluded at the moment they matter.
findings.direction: Separate the badge and the host label in space and keep labels facing the camera at a stable size.

findings.evidence: The CLIENT01 label is cropped by the left frame edge in _a ('IENT01'), _c and B-01.2_a, outside the title-safe area, and the label moves quickly across the frame.
findings.why: The label is clipped at the frame edge and outside the title-safe area.
findings.direction: Pin the label to the desk inside the safe area or keep the desk fully in frame.

findings.evidence: The caption plate sits over the focal subject: the user's body in B-01.1_b and _c, the lower safe in B-03.3 and B-03.4, the flashback tag in B-05.2_b, and the CA1 and web server area in B-09.2_b.
findings.why: The caption covers the focal action.
findings.direction: Place the caption in a consistent clear band and frame the focal subject above it.

findings.evidence: In the B-07.3 strip the camera swings between the labels, the vaults and the servers with large frame-to-frame changes. In the B-08.2 strip the move from the CA2 vault to WEB01 ends inside the label plane, and the framing jumps between tiles 4 and 6.
findings.why: The camera path is not controlled: it whips and clips through geometry. It reads like a jump, not a continuous motivated move.
findings.direction: Ease the camera along a clear path that leads with the capsule or cert, and keep it outside label geometry.

findings.evidence: A white ring and a white pill or bar appear beside the octagon plate inside the server after the capsule leaves, and outside the container box. A similar white ring or bar stays at the web server in B-07.3 and B-08.3. The locator box for KEY-RDP-PRIV is the dark safe, so this is a different object, which I could not positively identify.
findings.why: A key-like white shape stays outside the container. It may be a lock shackle or a public-key remnant, but nothing on screen says so, and it reads as a key left outside.
findings.direction: Make this object an unambiguous non-key shape, or remove it once its job is done, and let the PKI discriminator confirm the key trace.

findings.evidence: Vault and chassis interiors are lit by flat emissive colour with a soft dark shadow and no rim. Outside, only a single floor spot pool lights the shot. Darks are crushed, and the CA vault interiors read as uniform cyan or violet slabs.
findings.why: Close-up shots lack a motivated key and rim on the focal subject, so they look flat.
findings.direction: Add a visible key and a rim or back light on each focal subject and reduce the emissive wash.

findings.evidence: A hard black void with a visible finite floor edge fills 20 to 30% of many wide frames. The close-ups in B-03, B-04.3, B-04.4 and B-08.1 have no nearer or farther layers than the subject.
findings.why: The background layer is missing, so the set reads as a diorama on black, and the close-ups have no depth layering.
findings.direction: Extend the set with a horizon, fog or far geometry, and place foreground and background objects in the close-ups.

findings.evidence: The must-read tag "Issuing CA 1's own CA request" is about 7 px tall at 960x540. The cyan CA=true band on the request cannot be made out. The 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony' text is also tiny and sits over the vault.
findings.why: The only cue separating this request from the RDP request (PKI-S0R1-02) is not readable.
findings.direction: Frame the request and its tag large, with the band visible and a readable tag, for at least 1.5 s.

findings.evidence: The flashback reuses the live CA1 vault with the B-04.3 check text still drawn inside it, next to the root plinth.
findings.why: A continuity artefact from the present leaks into the flashback.
findings.direction: Clear the live check text from the vault in the flashback.

findings.evidence: The proof-of-possession beam is a rigid straight white rod from the safe to the capsule.
findings.why: It reads as a stick connector, not light.
findings.direction: Make it a soft, tapering light beam that fades in and out.
